controls.title: Intermediate root management group
controls.assertion: Every subscription sits in a management group below a single intermediate root management group, and no subscription is placed directly under the Tenant root group.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Export of the management group hierarchy (Management groups blade or az account management-group list) showing each subscription's parent.
controls.review_gate: Default: New subscriptions automatically default to the root management group when they're created. Moving a subscription changes which policies and role assignments it inherits; review inherited assignments at the target group before moving. A tree supports up to six levels, so keep it shallow.

controls.title: Default management group for new subscriptions
controls.assertion: The hierarchy setting for the default management group points to a dedicated management group (for example a sandbox group), so new subscriptions never land in the root management group.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Screenshot of the root management group's hierarchy settings showing the default management group, or the REST response from .../settings/default.
controls.review_gate: Default: By default, a new subscription that you add in a tenant becomes a member of the root management group. Configuring hierarchy settings requires resource provider operations on the root management group, so it needs elevated or root-scope access; choose a group whose policies suit an unreviewed new subscription.

controls.title: Authorization required to create management groups

controls.review_gate: Default: Any user, by default, can create new management groups in a tenant. After enabling, anyone who creates management groups needs the write permission on the root group; grant it only to the platform administrators. Compensating control that would allow the setting to be relaxed: None documented; enable the require-authorization setting.

controls.title: No standing access at root scope
controls.assertion: No user or group holds a standing role assignment at root scope (/) or on the Tenant root group, apart from an approved and documented exception.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Output of az role assignment list --scope / and on the root management group, with any exceptions recorded.
controls.review_gate: Default: No one has default access to the root management group. Microsoft Entra Global Administrators are the only users who can elevate themselves to gain access. Assignments at the root apply to every management group and subscription; removing the elevated User Access Administrator assignment requires the toggle or CLI, not the IAM page. controls.review_gate: Default: HTTPS-only redirect is not on by default. CIS: CIS Azure 2.0.0 9.2. Check for clients or health probes that call the app over plain HTTP.

Regulatory Compliance details for CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark 2.0.0

controls.title: App Service FTP disabled
controls.assertion: Every App Service app has FTP state set to Disabled, or FTPS only where FTP deployment is still required.
controls.evidence_to_collect: az webapp config show output showing ftpsState for every app, or the policy result for 'App Service apps should require FTPS only'.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; verify in the console. CIS: CIS Azure 2.0.0 9.10. FTPS only requires minimum inbound TLS 1.2 or higher; disable both FTP and FTPS if the app deploys another way. Compensating control that would allow the setting to be relaxed: FTPS only with minimum TLS 1.2, used only by a named deployment process.

Regulatory Compliance details for CIS Microsoft Azure Foundations Benchmark 2.0.0

controls.title: App Service basic auth publishing disabled
controls.assertion: Every App Service app has SCM and FTP basic authentication publishing credentials disabled.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Screenshot or export of each app's SCM Basic Auth Publishing Credentials and FTP Basic Auth Publishing Credentials settings.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; verify in the console. With basic authentication disabled, FTP/S deployment stops working; confirm deployments use Entra-based methods first. Compensating control that would allow the setting to be relaxed: FTPS only with minimum TLS 1.2 and publishing credentials reset after any staff change.

controls.title: Delete locks on production resource groups
controls.assertion: Every production resource group has a CanNotDelete (Delete) management lock, and only the Owner roster can remove locks.
controls.evidence_to_collect: az lock list output for production resource groups.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; verify in the console. Locks inherit to all resources, including storage accounts, and a Delete lock can make Azure Backup fail to clean up restore points; check backup resource groups before locking. A lock prevents deleting the resource, not deleting data inside it, and locks don't block subscription cancellation.

controls.title: Azure Backup protects VMs
controls.assertion: Every production VM is protected by Azure Backup in a Recovery Services vault with a documented backup policy.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Backup center or Recovery Services vault export listing protected VMs, their policy, and last successful backup time.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; verify in the console. Azure Backup is a paid service charged for protected instances and storage; check pricing before enabling.

sources.title: About Azure VM backup
What is Azure Backup?

controls.title: Recovery Services vault soft delete retention
controls.assertion: Every Recovery Services and Backup vault has soft delete on, with a recorded retention of at least 14 days.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Screenshot of each vault's Properties, Security settings, showing soft delete state and retention days.
controls.review_gate: Default: Soft delete is enforced by default (secure by default) with 14 days retention, configurable from 14 to 180 days; the state can no longer be modified from the portal. Retention beyond 14 days is charged; the default enforcement is in preview in some regions.

sources.title: Secure by Default with Soft Delete for Azure Backup

controls.title: Immutable vault enabled and locked
controls.assertion: Every Recovery Services vault holding production backups has immutability enabled and locked.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Screenshot of each vault's Properties, Immutable vault setting showing 'Enabled and locked'.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; the setting has three states (Disabled, Enabled, Enabled and locked), and enabled but unlocked can be disabled. Locking makes the setting irreversible and blocks operations such as reducing retention, so confirm backup policies first.

sources.title: Concept of Immutable Vault for Azure Backup

controls.title: Backup restore test recorded
controls.assertion: A restore of at least one VM or database backup is performed and recorded at least once a year, including date, item, and result.
controls.evidence_to_collect: The restore test record (ticket or document) with date, item restored, target, and outcome.
controls.review_gate: Default: None; this is a procedure, not a setting. Restore to an isolated location so the test does not overwrite production; Cross Region Restore can be used for drills.

sources.title: Create and Configure Recovery Services Vaults
Secure your Azure Key Vault

controls.title: Azure SQL point-in-time restore retention
controls.assertion: Every production Azure SQL database has point-in-time restore retention set deliberately (7 to 35 days) and backup storage redundancy recorded.
controls.evidence_to_collect: az sql db str-policy show output (retentionDays) and each database's backup storage redundancy.
controls.review_gate: Default: 7 days by default, configurable 1 to 35 days; backups use geo-redundant storage by default. Basic tier databases allow only 1 to 7 days; changing redundancy applies only to new backups.

sources.title: Automatic, Geo-Redundant Backups

controls.title: Budget with actual and forecast alerts per subscription
controls.assertion: Every subscription has a Cost Management budget with alerts on actual and forecasted cost sent to a monitored mailbox or action group.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Screenshot or export of each subscription's budgets, thresholds, and alert recipients or action groups.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; verify in the console. Budgets only notify; resources aren't affected and consumption isn't stopped. Budgets are evaluated about every 24 hours, so alerts can lag.

sources.title: Tutorial

controls.title: Cost anomaly alert per subscription
controls.assertion: Every subscription has a Cost Management anomaly alert that emails a named owner when an anomaly is detected.
controls.evidence_to_collect: Screenshot of each subscription's Cost Management alerts list showing an anomaly alert and its recipients.
controls.review_gate: Default: Not stated on the pages reviewed; verify in the console. Creating an anomaly alert requires the Cost Management Contributor role or higher; anomaly alerts are not available for Azure Government.
